quest.title: Buried Honor
quest.description: There seems to be something unusual about today's story...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x650, Mora x44000, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x10

talks.objective: Wait until morning the next day (08:00 – 10:00)
Meet up with the others at the game venue

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Looks like everyone's here. Before we begin, why don't we finish where we left off yesterday? There was an important decision to be made, yes? I'll pour everyone a cup of tea.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: I—Is that really the most important part, though, Clorinde? Paimon's more concerned about our current surroundings...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Heavy walls, cold railings, dim lights... This is obviously supposed to be a prison!

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I admire the work put into the set. Still, it's obvious the script writer has never paid a visit to the Fortress of Meropide.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: So this set... is going to be a part of the script?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, that is something I can neither confirm nor deny.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, anyone think Clorinde's smile is starting to look kinda scary...?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Well, whatever happens, we'll just have to push on. But first, we should really figure out what to do with this treasure.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: If we're worried about arousing suspicion because of our identity... Why don't we give ourselves a different name, just like Clorinde's Master did?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Yeah, it might be better to keep a low profile. As long as we're helping people, it doesn't matter who we are or what we're called.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Staring at me won't get you anywhere. Or, did you want some more tea?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, um... Paimon's good! Thanks!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why aren't you saying anything, Navia? Wait... What's that next to you?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Oh, this is the short sword Clorinde mentioned last night. I found it!

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Huh, I'm surprised you managed to track it down after all this time.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, I made sure to take good care of it! Considering the... circumstances in which you gave it to me, of course I had to keep it safe.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Anyway, where were we? Oh, right, I was just thinking about all the potential ways for us to break out of prison! We could dig a tunnel, or try to bribe the guards...?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: ...Wait, we haven't been thrown into prison yet, have we?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, it's only a matter of time! It pays to be prepared, just like how you should always have an umbrella on hand, even when it's sunny.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright! Paimon's made up her mind. Let's just give the treasure away!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon may have wanted to keep it, but if that's going to land us in prison somehow, Paimon will be too upset to enjoy her snacks.

choices.text: Turns out Paimon cares more about snacks than treasure.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: So, you've reached an agreement? Alright then, we can continue with the story.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, and we'll collect all the scattered pieces of treasure on the ground as well!

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Alright.

response.speaker: Game Master
response.text: You collect the treasure and make your way back to the capital with your bag of loot in hand.

talks.objective: Listen to Game Master Clorinde's narration

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: The city is still shrouded in a gloomy, oppressive atmosphere, but your spirits are surprisingly high.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: In places where sunlight struggles to reach, you generously share your wealth with the children, the elderly, and the poor in urgent need of help.

dialogues.speaker: Hunchbacked Old Lady
dialogues.text: Thank you, kind soul...

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: The elderly woman's look of gratitude follows you as you walk away, her eyes never leaving your back until you move entirely out of sight. However, there's still quite a bit of Mora remaining. It appears you haven't made much progress.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: (She's probably trying to tell us to speed this up. We need to hurry up so we can address the sorcerer problem...)

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Should we go find that man again at the square? He seemed like a pretty responsible guy. I'm sure he knows the people here far better than us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, good idea!

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Just as you start to make way to the square, intent on finding the man again, there's a voice...

dialogues.speaker: Serious Guard
dialogues.text: Please wait, distinguished guests.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Several strange guards suddenly call out to you. They run forward to meet you and proceed to politely pay their respects.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Greetings, gentlemen! Are we being invited for afternoon tea?

dialogues.speaker: Serious Guard
dialogues.text: Surely, you jest, my lady. That would not be our place. It is His Excellency the king, who requests to meet with you. Please come with us.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: You allow yourself to be led away by guards surrounding you on both sides.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: It's only when you begin to feel drops of water falling from the dungeon ceiling, and smell the stench of death and decay all around you, that you finally realize you've stepped into a completely different world.

dialogues.speaker: Serious Guard
dialogues.text: Stay here, and don't try anything funny.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: The guards lock the cell door and leave without looking back.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Wait, sir!

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Your voice echoes through the dark hall, but the only response you receive is the sound of water dripping from the ceiling.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Noooo... What should we do now...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Carve out a new path of fate with our own two hands, of course! I draw my weapon!

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: You reach toward your waist, but find nothing there. You now recall that your weapons were confiscated before the guards locked you in the cell... the bag of treasure along with them.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: What about that knife I hid in my boot?

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: ...When did you hide it in there?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: When I was thinking about digging a tunnel!

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Rejected. You failed to inform the GM of this course of action. Moreover, the guards would have conducted a thorough search before throwing you in prison.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: And the keys to the cell aren't anywhere to be seen?

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Correct. You don't even feel a lock hole on the cell door.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Well, there goes all our plans...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? Why are you the one saying "indeed"?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Because that statement holds true for me as well. This is where the script ends.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!? But that's a terrible ending!

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Hmm... Generally speaking, this should be the point where the script writer gives the players some kind of hint, or gives the GM some kind of code for how to move forward.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I mean, maybe they just really wanted us to be immersed in the feeling of being in prison? Like, they'll only show us the way out once we've grown truly and utterly desperate?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: That is a possibility.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If only there were desserts and tea in real prison... Oh, wait, guess that's kind of how the Fortress of Meropide works if you're lucky.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Oh, before I forget... Navia, the short sword you had with you earlier...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I took a closer look, and the craftsmanship doesn't appear to resemble anything from this era. If I remember correctly, that style was last in vogue several hundred years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Wait, Clorinde said that sword used to belong to her master, right? Does that mean... her master has been alive that long?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I doubt it. The way she went about things often made her seem childish more than anything. I'd say the sword was most likely an heirloom passed down over time.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hang on, a precious heirloom passed down to you by your master, and you gave it to me just like that? You weren't worried I might lose it?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Master left many things to me when she disappeared. There was the sword, an old key, and... a good amount of junk she probably just didn't want to take with her.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I gave you the sword back then... because I didn't want our friendship to end.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Wait, when did this happen exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: ...After the duel between Mr. Callas and myself.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Before that, Clorinde would have meals with us and even stay over at the Spina some days. She was on great terms with Papa as well.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: After the duel, though... There was a period of time where we simply didn't know how to face each other. She entrusted this sword to me, and never came back.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: We were both sad, and conflicted, and totally overthinking everything as a result, haha.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Whenever I looked at this sword, I couldn't help but wonder... If Ms. Petronilla had never introduced us to each other at that picnic, maybe part of the sadness I was feeling could have been avoided.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: ...Back then, it felt like I hadn't just lost a father, but a close friend as well.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: No one can change the past. The most important thing is that you two found your way back to each other and can enjoy things like this together.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: ...Yep, you're right!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, you two. I didn't mean to bring up any sad memories...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Think nothing of it. No one here is at fault.

dialogues.speaker: Noise From the Door
dialogues.text: *plop*

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Ah... Looks like the next part of our script is here.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: (Phew... Perfect timing. The situation was really starting to get desperate... and not just because of the prison thing...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: From Clorinde's face, Paimon really can't tell if it's good news or bad news...

choices.text: It speaks to her professionalism as a senior GM.

response.speaker: Game Master
response.text: Water continues to drip from the ceiling. In this lightless dungeon, you lack a reliable way to tell how much time has passed.

response.speaker: Game Master
response.text: Eventually, you get used to the unpleasant odor of straw, mold, and rust, and find yourselves alternating between fits of drowsiness and despair...

response.speaker: Game Master
response.text: Suddenly, you hear footsteps outside the door.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Heads up, everyone. Someone's coming.
Gather close, everyone, and keep your voice down.

choices.text: Maintaining a poker face takes true skill.

talks.objective: Talk to the person outside the cell

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: "Guard"
dialogues.text: I work as a guard in these dungeons, but my true identity is the same as your own — I'm also a Marechaussee Hunter.

dialogues.speaker: "Guard"
dialogues.text: Shh! I've already sent away the other guards, but if we make too much noise...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I understand. But, how can we be sure we can trust you?

dialogues.speaker: "Guard"
dialogues.text: The king has issued a formal decree. In light of the irrefutable proof of your crime, you're to be executed before tomorrow's sunrise. If you want to escape, it has to be now.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Executed...? We barely did anything!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Monsters appearing at the same location as the treasure... Could this entire thing have been a trap?

dialogues.speaker: "Guard"
dialogues.text: There will be time for speculation once we're out of here... As for my identity, I have no way to prove that to you just yet.

dialogues.speaker: "Guard"
dialogues.text: Infiltrating the capital was difficult, and finding a chance to speak with you has taken a lot out of me... I could go on, but I think we can all agree that now is not the time for details.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Well, it doesn't look like we have any other choice.)

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Have you seen our weapons anywhere, sir?

dialogues.speaker: "Guard"
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I brought them with me. They're just behind the door. Still, these weapons alone won't be enough to defeat the true enemy behind the scenes.

dialogues.speaker: "Guard"
dialogues.text: His faction is too powerful. The guards are all under his control, and he's even stationed a number of golems in various rooms throughout the palace.

dialogues.speaker: "Guard"
dialogues.text: To defeat him, you must find a secret vault. It is said that, within that vault, the Marechaussee Hunters of the past left behind a treasure with the power to defeat the sorcerer.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: You're not coming with us?

dialogues.speaker: "Guard"
dialogues.text: No, I'll remain in the dungeons to deal with the guards. I'll try my best to distract them so they don't go after you.

dialogues.speaker: "Guard"
dialogues.text: As long as my identity is not revealed, I'll be able to aid you when the final battle comes.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: In that case, please stay safe.

dialogues.speaker: "Guard"
dialogues.text: Thank you for your concern. I will do my utmost.

dialogues.speaker: "Guard"
dialogues.text: As for the location of the vault... Here. This map should lead you there.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Got it.

dialogues.speaker: "Guard"
dialogues.text: Alright, once I open the door, remember to stick close and refrain from making any noise. I'll lead you out of here as quickly as possible.

dialogues.speaker: "Guard"
dialogues.text: You now have the chance to restore the honor and legacy of the Marechaussee Hunters. So, please, get out there and reclaim what's ours!

dialogues.speaker: "Guard"
dialogues.text: And... Be sure to exercise caution.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: With the help of the guard, you successfully escape the dungeons. Your sense of despair and anxiety both seem to fade as you continue your quest.

talks.objective: Head to the secret vault and search for the treasure

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: This should be the place marked on the map.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: This bit of rock certainly looks suspicious!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, I'd say an investigation's in order then! Plus, if all else fails, we can just blow it up!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: (Kaboom—)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, you really meant that...

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Before you lies a serene stretch of open water, its surface shimmering a brilliant shade of sapphire blue.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, guess this means it's time for a swim!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: What's the matter?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: ...It's nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: As you step into the cave, you find yourself in an eerily quiet space. Before you lies a narrow passageway that appears to trail off endlessly into the distance.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, this must be where the treasure is hidden!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: But, this door is blocking our way in... Huh, it almost looks like it's been here for quite some time. I've got to hand it to the Tabletop Troupe. They really went all-out with the props...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Hmm...?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Huh? What have we got down here... A kind of mechanism connected to the door? It looks like we might have to arrange it into a certain pattern...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: (A pattern on a stone door... That's something Master mentioned before...)

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Huh? Something wrong, Clorinde?

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: ...After a long, difficult journey, you finally arrive at the location indicated by your map. It appears to be an ancient site of some sort, where treasure likely awaits.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Your surroundings are exceedingly quiet and serene, as if the secret that slumbers here has never once been disturbed. If you listen closely, you can almost convince yourself you can hear the sound of its calm, gentle breathing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aww... That description makes Paimon feel kinda bad for disturbing this place.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: We're doing this for the sake of the people, to free them from the evil sorcerer. I say it's time for this treasure to once again see the light of day.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Lyney's right. We need to keep going. The future of the kingdom depends on it.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: The next part of the story requires us to solve the puzzle, right? Let's start exploring the area.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: ...Yes. That should be fine.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: (Something feels off about all this. Guess I'll just have to improvise.)

talks.objective: Split up and look for clues

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: It worked!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Something just appeared... Some kind of new mechanism, maybe?

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: By solving the puzzles, you prove yourselves worthy of inheriting the secrets of the past.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: At the end of each puzzle, you're rewarded with...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: With...

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: A key...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Oh, must be the key to the big door...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: (This is... one of the Marechaussee Hunter keys that are passed down from generation to generation... It looks just like the one Master passed down to me.)

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: (It is said that four keys in total are required to form the final, complete key. And it seems like... we just collected three of them. That must mean...)

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Huh? What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: ...You hear a few strange noises. Suddenly, all the torches in the ruin go out at once.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Huh? Wh—What's going on? Did we fall into another trap?

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: For the sake of immersion, please close your eyes, everyone. Without the torches, the space is now completely dark, and you cannot see anything.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, Paimon can still see a little bit over here...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right, sorry...

response.speaker: Game Master
response.text: Suddenly... you hear the sound of footsteps pierce through the darkness.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Huh!? There's someone else here? Ugh... This is so unsettling! I can't see anything!
...Tch. I've been discovered, then?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Wait! That voice, it's...

response.speaker: Game Master
response.text: You recognize the voice as belonging to the "guard" who led you to this place. It appears he now covets the treasure for himself, and has come to stake his claim...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: (Oh, so this is just part of the script... Phew... Then I can probably relax.)

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Well, if we can't see anything, that means we can't fight to the fullest of our abilities. Should we... retreat for now?

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: (Judging by the way he's holding his sword... He must be a real Marechaussee Hunter. But, this isn't part of the script.)

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Retreat? Ha! That's not the Hunter way. If it's dark for us, then it's dark for him! We choose to fight!

response.speaker: Game Master
response.text: Your choice is noted. Please keep your eyes closed until I tell you the torches have been re-lit. This battle will be in the dark.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: You got it!

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Well then. Let us begin.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Is it over? Can we open our eyes now?

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: The enemy is strong and relentless, but the battle is nearing its end. The torches have not been re-lit...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: What about now?

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Final strike!

dialogues.speaker: "Guard"?
dialogues.text: Argh!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: W—Well? Did we get him?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Why isn't she answering...?)

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Uh... Clorinde?

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Warm fire flickers across the walls once again. Your vision is now clear.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: In an impressive display of courage, the four of you successfully defeat the uninvited guest.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: (That look in his eyes... It's like he became an entirely different person as soon as I defeated him.)

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Huh? Mr. Florian...?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: (...Oh, wait! We're supposed to be roleplaying. I should stay in character.)

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Ah, ahem...! Speak your name, guard. Why did you lead us here just to betray us?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: ...Is this treasure really more important to you than bringing peace to the kingdom?

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: Tch... What kingdom? What peace? Those were nothing but lies!

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: I, Florian, am a true Marechaussee Hunter, descended from Hunters of ages past.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: (So, he's also using his real name... Or wait, was that the name of his character from the very beginning...?)

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Then, I'm even more confused. If you truly are a Marechaussee Hunter, shouldn't you want to help us, just like you said before? Shouldn't we fight together for the sake of the people?

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: What do you know? In this day and age... There's no glory to be had as a Marechaussee Hunter.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: What's that supposed to mean?

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: My skills were passed down to me by my father. We lived a life of obscurity in the remote wilderness. Still, he devoted everything he had to being a Marechaussee Hunter.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: And what did he get in return? A life of poverty and pain... and a world that forgot all about him. When he died, not a single person came to mourn his passing!

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: The Marechaussee Hunters were the ones who saved this ci{RUBY#[D]Fontaine}ty! We're heroes! We deserve more recognition and respect than this!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: (Is he talking about how no one in the capital seems to remember the Hunters and their legacy? I didn't expect the script to contain this level of social criticism...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, that's why you want to take the treasure for yourself? You feel like you're owed fame and wealth?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: If you already knew where the treasure was located, why didn't you just come down here and take it?

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: Because... I still needed the final key...

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Ahem! Only a true Marechaussee Hunter is capable of passing through this final door.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: As someone who sought to hurt others for his own gain, Florian lost that right long ago.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Okay, but what is this treasure, anyway? We've got all the keys, right? So, can we just go in and take a look?

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: You're sure you want to go in?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've been talking about it for so long... Of course we want to see what's inside!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: And we've already defeated Florian, right? So, he won't try to take it from us anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: Tch... Pesky brats...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: (Watch yourself...)

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Then, let's open the door together.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Alright. Your choice of action is confirmed.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Clorinde takes out the keys from earlier and walks up to the heavy door.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Without anyone noticing, she takes out her own key and joins it with the others to form the final, required shape.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Before you, the door to the treasure, sealed and undisturbed for more than a hundred years, finally swings open.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: You hear the shrill wail of the door hinge as it rotates for the first time after years of disuse, almost like a sleeping giant letting out an extended yawn. You get the impression that the secrets buried behind this door might be just as heavy as the sound you just heard.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! It's open! C'mon, let's go in. Paimon wants to see what's inside!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Ooh, me too!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Uncovering hidden treasure is the most exciting part of adventuring! What do we have here... Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: A stone tablet... And some shabby weapons?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You... You call this a treasure vault? Looks more like an abandoned warehouse!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Maybe the Troupe ran out of budget at the end?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They provided a super immersive experience at the beginning, only to drop the ball at the most important part... They could have at least filled this place with cardboard Mora or something!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: ...Wait, I get it now! Paimon, this is the real Marechaussee Hunter "treasure"!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: Th—This is it? The Marechaussee Hunter treasure is just a stone slab and some broken swords? I can't believe it... I refuse to believe it!!

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: Argh! Argh... Ahhhh!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Woah! Are you okay?

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: The Marechaussee Hunter before you appears to suffer a serious mental breakdown. He needs to leave the room for a moment to collect himself.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: One of you seems to understand the significance of the treasure already. If the rest of you wish to follow suit, you may remain here in the meantime and explore your surroundings.

talks.objective: Talk to Florian at a distance

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: ...So, how are you doing? Feeling any better?

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: I... What just happened...?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Do you remember how you got here? Or what happened to your body just now?

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: I... I remember now... I brought you here... Because I wanted to... Ah! The explosives in the cave...!

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: You mean these?

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: ...Huh? How did you...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I could tell something was off the moment I stepped into this cave, so I kept an eye out. I've already dismantled the whole thing.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: Hah, so the strongest Champion Duelist in all of Fontaine saved the day once again... Guess I shouldn't be surprised. It would seem your skills as a Marechaussee Hunter are as sharp as ever...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I deserve some answers, don't you think? Tell me why you wanted to lure me here.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Everything you said earlier sounded like the truth. Luckily, your monologue was dramatic enough to convince my friends you were just roleplaying.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: I... I don't know... I just always felt like there was something in my heart that didn't belong to me... something agitated and angry... Tch, who knows, maybe it was my own anger all along... I could never really tell.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: The feelings about my father and the other Marechaussee Hunters are real. It just wasn't fair. I was angry... bitter that no one remembered them, or praised their accomplishments.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: I don't know when it started, but at some point, my anger came to completely consume me. At that point, I remembered the legend my father used to tell me, the one about the treasure...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: But if the treasure was all you cared about, why plant all those explosives? Wouldn't they just destroy the treasure, and bury you along with it?

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: Ah... I can't remember. My head is a mess... It felt like... there was this voice telling me to "eliminate the Hunters," but now, it's gone...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: ...From your description, I suspect you were dealing with a "Devorator."

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: ...A "Devorator"?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Oh, your Master... Ahem, your father, I mean, never talked about it? It was a kind of monster that was active several centuries ago.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: No, I've heard of it, I'm just not sure why you suddenly...

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: Wait, it can't be... The seal!

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: The seal?

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: My family... has served as Marechaussee Hunters for many generations. But the title and swordsmanship weren't the only things passed down over our line. There was a seal as well.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: My father instructed me to always watch over that seal and maintain it regularly. He said it had been passed down from a truly ancient age, and protecting it was our clan's most important duty.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: But, I neglected that duty after he died... I finally decided to come down and check on it one day, and that's where my memories become fuzzy...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: The Devorator would be a formidable adversary for any mortal being, even ones as capable as the Hunters.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: If you lacked the power to completely destroy it, you could easily fall prey to its influence and corruption. In light of this, some Marechaussee Hunters chose to seal the Devorator away in the hopes that a permanent solution would come with the passage of time.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: I heard it has the power to amplify the obsessions and desires in people's hearts, to the point where they overtake you entirely... Hah, it would seem I'm not just lacking in skill with a blade, but in mental fortitude as well...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: And yet, you were able to retrieve three of the four keys... If I remember correctly, each was entrusted to a respected and capable Hunter... How did you manage it?

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: ...One of them belonged to my father. The second I stole from a different Hunter... And the third, *sigh*... was one that I snatched while the person was on the way home from the tavern. I nearly died in that alley...

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: I know just how strong you are — it's as clear as day to everyone in Fontaine. I observed you from dusk to dawn, but could never find any opportunity to sneak up on you... I never even saw you drink a single glass of liquor...

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: The only way I could think to obtain that last key... was to lure you here using your hobby, and then... Ah, I get it now... That monster... It wanted to bury you here alongside the treasure...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: ...I won't comment on anything else, but the script was good.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: Hah... Well, I did pour my heart and soul into it...

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: The stories my father used to tell me... about the glory of the heroic Marechaussee Hunters... and how they came to be forgotten...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: It's more than just a story.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: You're proud to be a Hunter. You're still holding on to that part of yourself, no matter how small.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: Hah, I've done so many despicable things... I have nothing to be proud of...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Then explain the purpose of the "evil sorcerer" in your story.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Isn't he the true antagonist? The one who sought nothing but his own gain and used the people as pawns to attain it... In your heart of hearts, he was the one you truly wanted to defeat.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: B—But I've already tainted my sword. I no longer have any right to...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Wake up, Florian! Remember how you introduced yourself earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Do you really think the Hunters acted out of a desire for honor and glory, or to be loved and acknowledged by the people? What did your Father teach you about our order?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: You do not wield your sword for yourself, but to protect those you serve. There's nothing special about a blade. It's the intentions of the wielder that matter above all else.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Do you still not understand? Even after seeing the "treasure" for yourself? The contents of that room... they represent the true legacy the Hunters left behind.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: ...You're right. I... I am a Marechaussee Hunter. It's time for me to redeem — no, to finally serve the people I vowed to protect all along.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I wouldn't be so quick to push aside the need for redemption.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: ...I know. That's a charge I won't bother to defend myself against.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Good. Then come with me, and help me see this script through to the end.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: Huh? See the script through to the end? But... But there's no more script left.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Never finished it, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: No, I mean... I wrote the script with the sole purpose of luring you all here. There was no reason to write beyond this point...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Then we'll just have to keep writing it. The evil sorcerer still needs to be defeated.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: You mean... the Devorator? Uh... Are you saying I have to make up the rest of the script as we go along?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Is that really so hard? You've already written most of it. Surely you can write an ending where the Hunters win and justice prevails? I'll be there to help you, too.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: ...You aren't afraid your party will fall into danger?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I know what my friends are capable of, and they're all quite skilled. Besides, I need their help.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: Then... are you going to tell them the truth about all this?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Ah, I don't intend to spoil the fun. Sometimes, protecting dreams and fantasies is more important than exposing the truth, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: I implore you, everyone, please give me a chance to make up for all I've done. Allow me to fight alongside you, and defeat the evil sorc{RUBY#[D]Devorator}erer that threatens the peace and prosperity of all the people in this king{RUBY#[S]basement}dom.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, I say we let you join!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Sounds good to me, too. Everyone makes mistakes. What matters is what you do to make up for them.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I have no objections, but... Mr. Florian, do you even know how to defeat the evil sorcerer?

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: Hmm... When he took over my mind, I gained some insight into his thoughts. Every time I thought of the treasure... he reacted with a strong sense of fear.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? He's... afraid of the treasure? But there's nothing here except some broken weapons and the stone tablet...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: What if... The secret's hidden inside these weapons?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: GM, permission to "investigate"!

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: At first glance, the weapons appear absolutely ordinary, but as you observe them, you notice a faint energy emanating from within.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: These blades have slain countless monsters. Though it's been a long time since they were used in battle, their edges remain sharp, as if they're simply waiting for the next worthy Hunter to carry on their legacy.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: (So, basically, take these with us, right?)

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I'll take this weapon... Since it used to belong to Este. Maybe it'll find comfort in being held by someone who appreciates the arts.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Ah, good idea. I'll take Mr. Walter's bow, then. From one archer magician to another!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's gonna pick a cool weapon, too!

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: As you grip your weapons, you can almost feel the will of past Hunters coursing through your being. It's a feeling of courage, determination... a silent vow passed down from generation to generation that says, eradicate the monsters no matter the cost.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Mr. Florian, do you know where to find the evil sorcerer?

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: I was able to see his surroundings when our minds were connected. I believe he's currently hiding out at the chu{RUBY#[D]basement}rch in the king{RUBY#[S]my house}dom.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: We must be extremely careful. He's spent so long living among monsters that he has now taken the form of one. He will not be easily defeated.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then why don't we explore some more and try to find some higher-level gear? We don't want to just fight him and lose, right?

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: Oh, um...

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: No, we have to strike now! He was greatly weakened when I managed to break out of his control. If we let him rest, he might have time to escape.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I agree with Mr. Florian. We've got to act while we have the advantage. Don't forget — the people of the capital are counting on us.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Yeah, now that we've got a plan, there's no point in waiting. The longer this drags on, the worse it will be for everybody.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: Yes, yes! That's what's called...

response.speaker: Florian
response.text: Yes... That's exactly right!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, you've "persuaded" Paimon.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Mr. Florian, please lead the way.

response.speaker: Florian
response.text: Of course. Follow me!

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: (He had to set up so many scenes today, and now, he has to join in for this last part... I really don't envy his job.)

response.speaker: Game Master
response.text: *laugh* Finally... you decide to slay the evil sorcerer and bring peace back to the kingdom once and for all.

response.speaker: Game Master
response.text: As you walk away, you feel the gaze of the stone tablet at your back, as if all the Hunters of the past are wishing you success in the battle ahead and awaiting your triumphant return.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Hmm... Do you think this could be a trap?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Well, we have to investigate the court at some point, right? Meeting the king himself would be a fantastic opportunity to do that.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I say we go for it! If something happens, we'll just turn the whole place upside down!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, that sounds a little intense...

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: After a quick discussion, you nod to the guards and agree to follow. They lead you all the way to the audience hall of the palace.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Gilded tables line both sides of the hall. The space itself is adorned with all manner of expensive antiques, glass shelves, and silver candlesticks. The items appear quite ordinary in size and dimension, yet their presence somehow makes the emptiness of the hall feel even more surreal and ominous.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow... It's so luxurious!

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: The elderly king, clad in a magnificent robe sits upon the deep crimson throne before you.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: He wears above his head a majestic crown, with a gemstone the size of a bird's egg set right at the very front. As you observe it, you see a complex pattern of light reflect off its surface.
They're here, your majesty.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: A man dressed in dark clothes, likely a minister, shields his mouth with his hands and bends down to whisper a few words to the king.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: After a moment, he lowers his hands and stands back up. His gaze shifts to fixate on your group, but he does not move from his place at the king's side.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: (The king does not appear entirely aware of his surroundings. The man by his side, though... We should keep a close eye on him.)

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: The king remains still, and says nothing. The Minister is the one who speaks.

dialogues.speaker: Prime Minister
dialogues.text: Esteemed guests, allow me to thank you for coming to our faraway kingdom. Unfortunately, His majesty the king finds himself quite exhausted from work, so please allow me, his prime minister, to welcome you in his stead.

dialogues.speaker: Prime Minister
dialogues.text: I've heard tell that your group, the Marechaussee Hunters, used your exceptional ability with the sword to repel the monsters near the capital. Such a great deed deserves to be rewarded.

dialogues.speaker: Prime Minister
dialogues.text: However, seeing that I was not fortunate enough to observe such a feat with my own eyes, you'll forgive me for seeking to verify the truth by speaking to you myself...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, we've got nothing to hide! You brought us here to talk, right? So, we'll just explain what happened.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...The golems' blades were so powerful, they could cut down trees in a single swipe! It took a lot of effort to defeat them, even for trained swordsmen like us!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, that was enough details, right? Believe us, now?

dialogues.speaker: Prime Minister
dialogues.text: Hmm... Your account does indeed match those of the survivors. Since you were the ones who defeated the monsters, that must mean... You are also in possession of the treasure they stole?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, we did take the treasure, but...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: (How did he know about the treasure?)

dialogues.speaker: Prime Minister
dialogues.text: Ah, then I must ask that you return it at once. It belongs to the kingdom.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Wait, but didn't you just say that our great deed deserved a reward? Shouldn't the treasure be considered a part of that?

dialogues.speaker: Prime Minister
dialogues.text: Hehe... Yes, yes. That was indeed what I said, but you seem to have forgotten a very important distinction.

dialogues.speaker: Prime Minister
dialogues.text: Only that which is freely given by the king can be considered a reward. Taking the rightful wealth of a kingdom without said permission, on the other hand... is a crime.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: But that's completely unreasonable!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, that makes no sense! If it weren't for us, the treasure would still be buried underground somewhere!

dialogues.speaker: Prime Minister
dialogues.text: Maybe so, yet the fact remains... You tried to dispose of the treasure without reporting it to the court and without receiving permission, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um...

dialogues.speaker: Prime Minister
dialogues.text: What, no answer? Surely you're not insinuating that you, a group of legendary Marechaussee Hunters, sought to take the treasure for yourselves?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Argh, well, what about the king? Is he just going to let this guy talk for him for the whole time?

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Clad in his magnificent robe, the king remains seated with his hands resting on either side of the throne, his posture rigid and unmoving. He stares forward with an empty look in his eyes, completely unmoved by the events before him.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: (From the look of things... could the Prime Minister be the evil sorcerer? Or... could both the king and the Prime Minister have fallen under the evil sorcerer's control?)

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I would like to observe the number of guards stationed in the hall.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: The guards in the palace appear fully armed, their expressions solemn. Sensing the tense atmosphere in the room, they stand at the ready, each with a hand placed upon the hilt of their sword, as if prepared to draw their weapons and surround you at a moment's notice.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: There goes my plan to turn the whole place upside down, I guess.

dialogues.speaker: Prime Minister
dialogues.text: It appears we've been visited by nothing more than a group of ill-intentioned imposters... What a pity. Guards, take them away, and throw them in the dungeons.

dialogues.speaker: Prime Minister
dialogues.text: Before I decide your fate, however, I must first determine whether you have any accomplices outside the court...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Can't we try to slip away? Or maybe start some kind of riot?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: But if we try to fight the guards right now...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Don't worry, at least we've figured out who's behind all this. Let's just play it by ear. If you're scared, Paimon, just hold my hand.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You can have my hand, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aww, thanks you guys...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Ah, they're back!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That took a while.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: ...Ahem.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: Oh, uh...

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: Ahem! My fellow Marechaussee Hunters, please forgive me, for I have sinned...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: (Tone it down...)

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: (S—Sorry...)

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: After crossing swords with you and witnessing your courage in battle, I have rediscovered my true self and regained my pride as a Marechaussee Hunter.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: (Oh! Do I smell a redemption arc?)

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: I confess... I was brainwashed by the evil sorcerer. He asked me to lure you here so he could bury you in this cave...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That little... Wait... You're saying all of that wasn't you, but the evil sorcerer?

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: That's right. He's adept at manipulating the hearts and minds of the people... I fell under his influence because I did not possess a strong enough sense of will.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph! And how are you going to prove that you're a changed man? We're not going to fall for the same trap twice!

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: Um...

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: To be perfectly honest, I only came to my senses after seeing the "treasure." It reminded me of my father's past teachings.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: The "treasure" was actually...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: The names of all the Marechaussee Hunters from ages past and their weapons?

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: Wait, you... already know?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Of course! Don't underestimate a veteran roleplayer's exploration skills! Wait, I mean, Marechaussee Hunter Navia's exploration skills!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: We just finished reading through the content of the stone tablet.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: That tablet recorded the lives of some fascinating people. For example, this Marechaussee Hunter called "Este"...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: She inherited the responsibilities of the Golden Hunter and passed judgment on many people. But, in private, she had a very easygoing personality. Her favorite pastime was singing and dancing with her friends, and she was said to have a beautiful voice.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: So she was just like you!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Oh, you really think so...?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Well... when you put it that way, I suppose I also have a few things in common with this "Walter."

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Working as an executioner, he supposedly used a countless number of tricks to confound his enemies in battle. If only I could've seen the feats of magic he pulled off back then...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Their lives were all so exciting! You could write so many cool books about their accomplishments. How could they have all been forgotten?

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: Because... they chose to be.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: To hunt monsters that only appear in the shadows, you must also operate in the dark. To be a Marechaussee Hunter is to willingly give up on wealth and fame.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Then this stone tablet must have been left behind by their companions.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: That's right. Few Marechaussee Hunters ever revealed their identity to the public. They always protected the ci{RUBY#[D]Fontaine}ty from the shadows.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: The only time they spoke of their accomplishments would be at night, when they gathered with their fellow Hunters in front of the bonfire to share stories of the monsters slain by their hand.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: So... this tablet was created not so that the Hunters would be remembered by the people, but so that they would be remembered by each other.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No wonder this place was so well-hidden...

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: You regard the stone tablet in solemn silence. The names of your comrades etched onto its surface serve as a reminder that you are never truly alone.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: The tablet proves that, although a Hunter walks a shrouded path, it is not a solitary one. There will always be those who walk beside you, a fact that remains as true today as in ages long past.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Their legacies shall continue to be passed down from generation to generation, as everlasting as the stone onto which their names are carved.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: (Father... You once told me that I should seek out the "treasure" if I ever became lost. So this is what you wanted me to find...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I've decided to trust you, Florian.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: Thank you, my friend... You are very kind.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'd like to do an insight check on him.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: His eyes are sincere, and his words ring true. You can tell that every word he spoke just now came from the bottom of his heart.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Um... Just between the two of us, could you tell me what it was like to be the Geovishap's pet?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: It was nothing special, really. Geovishaps don't understand the concept of a "pet." So, basically, it just headbutted me whenever I entered its territory.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: And that... hurt?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Yeah, it hurt. What, something you want to experience for yourself?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I'm good, thanks!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: The names on the tablet...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: The old and broken weapons...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is the "treasure" supposed to be...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: "Walter"...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Found something here, too.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I'd like to try to hit him with my sword.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Your strike is successful.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hah, you're facing a veteran Marechaussee Hunter. You don't stand a chance!

dialogues.speaker: "Guard"?
dialogues.text: Tch...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I—Is he still standing? Goodness, he sure has a lot of HP...
